_about: The hand-kept half of the site's Rust tracker (site/rust/). rust/tools/progress.py adds the counted half and writes site/rust/progress.json. Status is one of: done, live, active, next, parked, later.
goal: games against the AI that cost a fraction of the server's CPU: one-on-one games against the AI with Pioneer and Standard decks, decided in milliseconds.

phases.name: Contracts and measurement
phases.text: State traces and fingerprints, decision logs, the wire conformance suite and the AI speed bench. A seeded game replays to the same trace twice in a row.

phases.name: Rust gateway
phases.text: playmat-gateway sits in front of the Java server and routes each group of calls to Java, Rust, or both to compare. It has carried every connection on the public server since 4 Nov 2026.

phases.name: Platform services
phases.text: Card search, deck checks, deck sync, deck import by link, staff records and support in Rust, each answered alongside Java and compared.

phases.name: Career economy
phases.text: The Career's records and level track are built and compared; payouts wait until the AI work lands.

phases.name: Rules engine and card pipeline
phases.text: A Rust rules engine with cheap copies, and a transpiler that turns XMage's Java card files into data. Every card is checked against Java with shadow games. The first pool is in: all 42 Pioneer and Standard school decks and the 24 meta decks the AI plays, plus the Modern meta decks and the starter decks. Next: every Pioneer-legal card.

phases.name: Rust AI
phases.text: Whole-turn playouts on engine copies, deciding in milliseconds. It plays the AI's seat in Java's games for listed players, and the whole game when the Rust engine hosts it.

phases.name: Retire Java
phases.text: Started with AI games: since 11 Nov a one-on-one game against the AI can run on the Rust engine with no Java game behind it, for players who turn it on in Settings. Tables between people, tournaments, drafts and solo come once the pool covers the formats people play.

steps.name: Measure
steps.text: The server logs what each Rust AI game costs: Java's game thread, the trace, and the Rust copy.
steps.gate: A week of production cost lines

steps.name: Fidelity
steps.text: Every card of the 24 Pioneer and Standard meta decks in the engine, with a shadow game for each pairing: 287 of 288 match, and Java didn't finish the other.
steps.gate: A week of production AI games that follow Java to the end

steps.name: Views in Rust
steps.text: What the client sees (views, prompts and the game log) built by the Rust engine and compared with Java's.
steps.gate: Zero view differences on a week of real games

steps.name: Human side and host
steps.text: A Rust host for the whole game: skip settings, priority timers, mulligans, concede, reconnect, best-of-three, spectators, replays and the Career's pay.
steps.gate: The live client tests pass against a Rust-hosted game

steps.name: Rollout
steps.text: Rust-hosted games for listed players, and for every player who turns on "Play on the Rust engine" in Settings, live since 11 Nov 2026. Then every AI duel whose decks qualify, by default.
steps.gate: A week with no game lost to the host, then the default

steps.name: Then
steps.text: More of the Pioneer pool, and what still plays on Java only: the solo tools, advice and practice tools.

measures.label: CPU per AI search node
measures.note: 84 seeded duels with the Pioneer and Standard school decks, one thread. The Rust AI searches fewer nodes per decision, so the decision times are the fairer comparison.

measures.label: A whole game replayed by the Rust engine

cost.note: CPU seconds per AI game with real decks. Java alone: its own AI. With the Rust AI: the AI's thinking moves to the Rust copy, and what's left is Java hosting the game.
